content.text: Apache Maven is an open-source software project management and build tool used primarily for Java-based projects. It simplifies the process of:
Definition: Maven is a project management tool that uses a declarative approach (via pom.xml) to manage builds, dependencies, and documentation.
Before tools like Maven, developers had to:

items: Create custom scripts to build the project
Share libraries manually across teams and environments
Deal with IDE inconsistencies in directory naming (e.g., WebContent, web, Web Pages)
Automates build tasks via lifecycle phases
Handles both compile-time and run-time dependencies (including transitive ones)
Minimizes manual downloads and network usage

content.text: pom.xml is the heart of a Maven project.
Maven pulls required libraries (JARs) from remote repositories and stores them locally.

items: Direct dependencies: Required by the project
Transitive dependencies: Required by project dependencies

items: Clean – Cleans up the previous build (e.g., target/ folder)
Default – Actual build process (compile, test, package)

content.text: Maven automatically runs previous phases before the one you specify.

items: Deploying to a server or repository

rows: Triggers required previous build phases automatically
Manages a project from creation to deployment
Handles dependency resolution and documentation generation
Simplifies repetitive tasks (compile, test, package, deploy)
Works seamlessly across IDEs like Eclipse, NetBeans, IntelliJ
Easily integrates with Nexus or Artifactory for central repo management
Reuse configuration and plugin logic across multiple projects

content.text: A Java application Infycart uses DataBaseUtil to connect to a MySQL database.

items: Uses DriverManager.getConnection() to establish DB connection
Singleton pattern used to share one connection instance
Requires log4j.jar as a compile-time dependency
Must be added to the classpath
